generated.title: M7.0 Earthquake Strikes Remote Northern Tibet
generated.description:
A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck a remote area of the Tibetan Plateau, 191 km east-northeast of Nagqu, China, on October 22, 2026 at 14:33 UTC (22:33 local time), at a depth of 18 km, according to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS). The event data has been reviewed by USGS. USGS's moment tensor shows normal faulting, the kind of faulting associated with the east-west stretching of the Tibetan Plateau.

USGS issued an orange PAGER alert for this earthquake. The orange level comes from the modeled estimate of economic losses; the modeled estimate for fatalities is at the yellow level. PAGER is a modeled estimate of potential impact, not a report of what actually happened. In the information we reviewed, no casualties or damage had been confirmed by authorities. This may change as more information becomes available.

Magnitude is the USGS value (Mww). Other agencies may publish different preliminary magnitudes for the same earthquake.

Official event page: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/eventpage/us6000u43g
